key: Hunger is the worst of diseases, the body the greatest of pains; if one knows this truly, that is Nirvana, the highest happiness.
s: In the chapter on happiness, after a verse on passion, the verse ends on Nirvana; the Theravāda commentary, on verse 203, reads hunger as chief of diseases, since others pass once treated while hunger needs treating always, and the body as the five aggregates.

evidence.words: Tattha jighacchāparamā rogāti yasmā añño rogo sakiṃ tikicchito vinassati vā tadaṅgavasena vā pahīyati, jighacchā pana niccakālaṃ tikicchitabbāyevāti sesarogānaṃ ayaṃ paramā nāma. Saṅkhārāti pañca khandhā.
evidence.gloss: There, 'hunger is the chief of diseases': because any other disease, once treated, perishes or is abandoned for the time being, whereas hunger must be treated at all times, it is called the chief of the remaining diseases. 'Saṅkhārā' means the five aggregates.
